experiences.name: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park
experiences.description: Experience the iconic Japanese hanami (flower viewing) tradition beneath hundreds of blooming cherry trees. The park's famous weeping cherry tree is illuminated at night, creating a magical atmosphere. Pack a picnic bento box and join locals in celebrating the arrival of spring. Perfect for families with open spaces for children to play.

experiences.name: Senso-ji Temple and Nakamise Shopping Street
experiences.description: Visit Tokyo's oldest and most significant Buddhist temple, dating back to 628 AD. Walk through the iconic Kaminarimon Thunder Gate and explore the vibrant Nakamise shopping street lined with traditional snacks, souvenirs, and crafts. Families can try on yukata rentals and participate in omikuji fortune-telling. A deeply immersive cultural and historical experience.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore Japan's most famous food market and indulge in fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), grilled scallops, and matcha treats. Join a guided family-friendly walking tour to learn about Japanese culinary traditions, seafood culture, and the art of sushi-making. Many stalls offer tastings and hands-on experiences for children.

experiences.name: Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Park
experiences.description: A profoundly moving and educational experience for families, the Peace Memorial Museum chronicles the events of August 6, 1945, and promotes a message of world peace. Walk through the Peace Memorial Park, see the iconic A-Bomb Dome, and fold paper cranes at the Children's Peace Monument. An essential historical and cultural visit that resonates deeply with visitors of all ages.
experiences.location: Peace Memorial Park, Naka Ward, Hiroshima

experiences.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Monkey Park
experiences.description: Stroll through the ethereal bamboo forest of Arashiyama, one of Japan's most photographed landscapes, especially stunning during cherry blossom season when petals drift through the towering green stalks. Afterward, hike up to Iwatayama Monkey Park where children can hand-feed wild Japanese macaques with panoramic views of Kyoto below. Combine with a rickshaw ride for a full family adventure.
